places.description: Luxe quarters with city views in a chic high-rise hotel offering 10 restaurants & an upscale spa.
places.name: Mandarin Oriental, Tokyo

sources.shortName: 12 Best Hotels in Tokyo, Japan
sources.snippet: Prestigious and well positioned in the financial district, the Mandarin Oriental, Tokyo, the crown jewel of Nihonbashi Mitsui Tower, is one of the city's finest, most timeless hotels with high-end amenities galore. After a morning of sightseeing, the 37th-floor spa beckons relaxation seekers with rejuvenating treatments. Guests also rave about the rooms, which mix contemporary Japanese charm with skyline views, the on-site dining options — ranging from the famous Tapas Molecular Bar to French fine dining — and the elegant atmosphere.

sources.shortName: The Best Luxury Hotels In Tokyo
sources.snippet: Set northeast of central Tokyo station, near the swish Ginza shopping district and rambling grounds of the Imperial Palace, the Mandarin Oriental Tokyo has a glossy, international appeal to it, suitable for business travellers as much as those seeking leisure. The amenities are crowd-pleasing too, especially if you have children in tow, with a pizza bar on the 38th floor and spa treatment rooms overlooking the city for parental downtime.

sources.shortName: 37 Best Hotels in Tokyo for Ryokan Stays and High-Rise Views
sources.snippet: $$$ | Gold List 2021, 2024 Readers' Choice Awards 2018, 2021. Rising to the upper floors of the Nihonbashi Mitsui Tower, the 38th-floor lobby is like a gallery to the capital’s best angles. It’s the same in the rooms: No matter the category, the view is paramount from your tranquil retreat in the sky, as the frenetic financial district eases down below and, on cloudless days, Mount Fuji glistens in the distance.

sources.shortName: Best hotels in Tokyo | Telegraph Travel
sources.snippet: A timeless presence standing sleekly on Tokyo’s high-rise skyline, with sophisticated design, a whole constellation of fine dining possibilities, and, on clear days, epic views of Mount Fuji floating above the sprawling megalopolis.

places.description: Plush rooms & suites in a posh hotel offering acclaimed dining, plus a luxe spa with an indoor pool.
places.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Tokyo

sources.shortName: The Best Luxury Hotels In Tokyo
sources.snippet: Set in the heart of Roppongi, electric with nightlife, shopping and some of the city’s finest wagyu restaurants, the Ritz-Carlton has jaw-dropping views across Tokyo – the 45th-floor lobby lounge alone will have you reaching for your camera. Neighbouring Tokyo Tower, one of the capital’s landmarks with its orange Eiffel Tower-esque façade, is right outside your window when you dine at Michelin-starred Azure 45; even the pool brings vistas over the cityscape.

sources.shortName: 37 Best Hotels in Tokyo for Ryokan Stays and High-Rise Views
sources.snippet: This five-star hotel commands the top nine floors of Tokyo's second-tallest building—and windows place you at eye-level with Tokyo’s second-tallest structure, Tokyo Tower. Inside is no less humble, and restaurants and bars often feel rich and handsome with dark finishes, plush chairs, and slick views. Courtesy Hoshino Resorts

sources.shortName: 12 Best Hotels in Tokyo, Japan
sources.snippet: Spanning the top nine floors of the 53-story Midtown Tower in Roppongi, the Ritz-Carlton, Tokyo, is a great place for luxury lovers — especially those with kids. The concierge will happily arrange babysitting and a stroller to use during your stay. There’s a little alcove off the lobby with books and toys for kids.

sources.shortName: Best hotels in Tokyo | Telegraph Travel
sources.snippet: There’s high-rise and then there’s this: a luxury hotel perched atop the tallest building in the world’s most populous metropolis. It’s got Michelin-starred dining, seamless service and a calmness that contrasts brilliantly with the chaos 50 floors below.

places.description: Luxe high-rise hotel offering 3 elegant restaurants, a hip bar & a spa, plus an indoor pool.
places.name: The Peninsula Tokyo

sources.shortName: 12 Best Hotels in Tokyo, Japan
sources.snippet: Fans of sightseeing who plan to visit the Imperial Palace couldn’t pick a better location than The Peninsula Tokyo, a classic luxury stay steps from the Hibaya entrance. As you’d expect from the beloved brand (and the price point), every detail is carefully considered and executed flawlessly — from the spacious suites and sanctuary spa with a panoramic pool and bespoke treatments to the too-pretty-to-eat treats at afternoon tea and cultural activities such as learning to make glass wind chimes to the unparalleled white-glove service.

sources.shortName: The Best Luxury Hotels In Tokyo
sources.snippet: With architecture inspired by a rose-coloured lantern, abstract calligraphic artworks on the walls and views over the Imperial Palace across the road, this luxury hotel has Japanese tradition woven into its design. The Peninsula’s central Yurakucho location close to the high-end stores of Ginza. Inside, you’ll find 314 decadent rooms and suites, a rooftop restaurant, two ballrooms and a wedding chapel.

sources.shortName: 37 Best Hotels in Tokyo for Ryokan Stays and High-Rise Views
sources.snippet: One of Tokyo’s most iconic pieces of art is not in fact in one of its museums—it’s in the lobby of the Peninsula Tokyo; the Lying Dragon Gate (which looks like a giant wooden eye) attracts legions of curious outsiders who sneak in for a glance. And when they walk through the lobby, they are immediately ensconced in the coziness of the entry’s dark wood and heavy fabrics. Although the hotel is Japanese inspired, the Peninsula Tokyo incorporates many pan-Asian elements—gilt finishes, flower petal motifs on the carpets, and cherry wood panelling, to name a few.

sources.shortName: 11 best hotels in Tokyo
sources.snippet: Why stay here: Minutes from the world-famous Ginza shopping district, enjoy the hotel's heritage charm while you shop.

places.description: Polished quarters in an upmarket hotel offering 4 restaurants, a lounge & spa, plus an indoor pool.
places.name: Conrad Tokyo

sources.shortName: 12 Best Hotels in Tokyo, Japan
sources.snippet: A well-established business hotel with a first-class lineup of offerings for leisure travelers, the Conrad Tokyo — a winner in our most recent World’s Best Awards — covers 10 floors of the Tokyo Shiodome Building. Its sky-high perch means stunning panoramas from innovative Chinese and contemporary French restaurants, TwentyEight Bar & Lounge, the 82-foot spa pool, and the generously sized rooms or suites. Pro tip: Specific room categories can access the executive lounge, which serves complimentary breakfast, afternoon tea, snacks, and evening cocktails.

sources.shortName: The Best Luxury Hotels In Tokyo
sources.snippet: Next door to Hamarikyu Gardens, one of Tokyo’s most atmospheric landscaped green spaces, the Conrad keeps things classically luxurious with wood and white rooms and gentle botanical print on carpets. The buzzy bar space, overlooking the city below and steely Tokyo Bay, is a meeting place for locals and visitors alike, while the China Blue restaurant is a moodily lit space perfect for a romantic dinner, chased down with a bottle from the walk-in cellar.

sources.shortName: Best hotels in Tokyo | Telegraph Travel
sources.snippet: A shiny lipstick-red lacquer sculpture sets a playful modern tone at the ground-floor entrance of the Conrad Tokyo – before ear-popping elevators transport visitors to an elegant, urban, cloud-brushing haven of clean-lined design, contemporary art and restaurants-with-a-view at the apex of a skyscraper in a central business district.

sources.shortName: 37 Best Hotels in Tokyo for Ryokan Stays and High-Rise Views
sources.snippet: $$ | Readers' Choice Awards 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024. When it opened in 2005 in the Shiodome area, Conrad Tokyo neatly fit in among the pantheon of international luxury brands. Almost two decades later, it remains as eye-catching as ever.

places.description: Posh rooms & suites, some with Mount Fuji views, in a ritzy hotel offering an indoor pool & a spa.
places.name: Park Hyatt Tokyo

sources.shortName: Best hotels in Tokyo | Telegraph Travel
sources.snippet: Among Tokyo’s top (and best-loved) hotels, the Park Hyatt is a five-star legend, renowned for its starring role in Lost in Translation alongside Bill Murray and Scarlett Johansson. It offers flawless service, elegant design, views of Mount Fuji and one of the world’s most atmospheric cocktail bars.

sources.shortName: 11 best hotels in Tokyo
sources.snippet: Why stay here: Easily the most famous Park Hyatt of the bunch, the Park Hyatt Tokyo offers stellar service, delicious food and tranquility high above the bustle of Japan's capital.

sources.shortName: 16 Best Hotels in Tokyo
sources.snippet: Whereas the Grand Hyatt attracts a clientele that enjoys being in the middle of the action, the Park Hyatt cultivates a lower profile, buffered from the hustle and bustle of Tokyo by its slightly out-of-the-way location in west Shinjuku, remedied, naturally, by a free 5-minute shuttle bus to Shinjuku Station. Gaining worldwide fame after its debut in Lost in Translation, the hotel has gorgeous rooms, all with stunning views (those facing east toward Shinjuku’s night lights are the most popular) and walk-in closets. Hotel highlights include a 2,000-book library, the ever-popular New York Grill with its famed weekend brunch and expansive list of Californian wines (including hard-to-find vintages), free use of bicycles, spa and fitness facilities that include sun-lit lap pool and gym offering yoga and other classes all free of charge.

sources.shortName: The 10 Best Hotels in Tokyo, Japan (with Prices)
sources.snippet: The Park Hyatt Tokyo’s starring role in Sophia Coppola’s inimitable film Lost in Translation rocketed it to icon status—but even without its Hollywood cachet, the five-star sleep holds up to its reputation as one of the best stays in Tokyo. Yes, the interiors are timeless, the 177 guest rooms tranquil aeries with heart-stopping views of the sweeping metropolis (on a good day, and from the best rooms, you can spot Mount Fuji), but it’s the flawless service that truly sets it apart—whether you’re luxuriating in a massage at the 45th-floor spa, ordering sake and Japanese sirloin at the now-famous 52nd-floor New York Grill and Bar, or recharging over cakes and tea in the bamboo garden after a day of sightseeing. Explore More: See hotel details | See all Tokyo, Japan hotels

places.description: Refined lodging with contemporary rooms & Italian dining, plus city views, a spa & an indoor pool.
places.name: Aman Tokyo

sources.shortName: The Best Luxury Hotels In Tokyo
sources.snippet: Besides the exceptional treatments, including world-best massages and Shinto purification rituals, the mirror-like pool overlooking the city is a perfectly tranquil place to watch the sky turn sunset-pink. Rooms are dressed in contemporary Japanese stylings, with light woods, crisp white sheets and sliding shoji paper doors. Sample a parade of traditionally prepared Tokyo Bay sushi – omakase-style – at eight-seater Musashi by Aman.

sources.shortName: 37 Best Hotels in Tokyo for Ryokan Stays and High-Rise Views
sources.snippet: $$$ | Gold List 2019, 2022 Readers' Choice Awards 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2024. Japan’s capital is many things—sprawling, neon-lit, nocturnal—but one word not often used to describe it is relaxing. I registered this dissonance approximately an hour after I last checked into Aman Tokyo.

sources.shortName: 12 Best Hotels in Tokyo, Japan
sources.snippet: The budget-unencumbered crowd loves Aman Tokyo — and Travel + Leisure editors and readers agree. The exclusive five-star retreat atop Otemachi Tower in Chiyoda City earned the coveted top spot of the best hotel in Tokyo in our most recent World’s Best Awards. “It’s a perfect city hotel,” says Elizabeth Rhodes, T+L senior editor, who stayed at the polished property in May 2024.

sources.shortName: Best hotels in Tokyo | Telegraph Travel
sources.snippet: Aman Tokyo is an escapist urban sanctuary floating above the city, spanning the cloud-brushing apex of a 38-storey skyscraper. Minimalist interiors of wood, paper and stone offer a soothing modern riff on Japan’s traditional design heritage, alongside spacious light-flooded suites offering bathing with a view.

places.description: Streamlined rooms in a polished hot spring hotel featuring a French/Japanese restaurant.
places.name: HOSHINOYA Tokyo

sources.shortName: The Best Luxury Hotels In Tokyo
sources.snippet: Modelled after a traditional Japanese ryokan (inn), Hoshinoya has an intimate feel unlike many of the other best hotels in Tokyo. Tatami mat floors line the hallways and bedrooms (you remove your shoes on arrival); the rooftop onsen-style bath feels almost meditative; the basement restaurant with private dining rooms turns out exceptional Japanese-French cuisine. Optional activities, from sake tastings to tea ceremonies, sumo training viewing to gagaku musical performances, give insight into Japanese culture.

sources.shortName: 12 Best Hotels in Tokyo, Japan
sources.snippet: The on-site experiences make a stay here so memorable — so don’t overload your sightseeing schedule. Upon entering Hoshinoya Tokyo, a wave of all-encompassing zen washes over you, making it easy to forget you’re staying in the middle of the business district of a booming metropolis. An urban ryokan for travelers who want to experience Japanese cultural traditions in a contemporary setting, the five-star refuge features serene rooms outfitted with tatami mats and wooden soaking tubs.

sources.shortName: 15 Best Boutique Hotels in Tokyo (2025): Tokyo Edition, Aman Tokyo, & More
sources.snippet: Top amenities: Open-air rooftop onsen, tranquility, tatami-lined tea roomsWhat’s nearby: Close proximity to Otemachi Station with access to plentiful metro connections. Before opening in 2016 in the lesser-known business district of Otemachi, this homegrown hotel chain drilled almost a mile under Tokyo’s concrete to tap into a hot spring and draw its mineral-rich water. The 17-story tower has 84 rooms and manages to feel more like a dozen ryokans than it does one hotel.

sources.shortName: 10 of the best hotels in Tokyo, from charming ryokans to Japanese onsen retreats
sources.snippet: Best for: cultural immersionLeave the city, and your shoes, behind as you step onto the tatami floors of this skyscraper ryokan. It’s a low-lit retreat of shoji screen doors and incense-scented air, with a second-floor lobby that includes a little salon for tea ceremonies. The 84 rooms are spread across the next 14 floors, with each level centred around a traditional ochanoma lounge serving teas, sake and house-made snacks.

places.description: Chic rooms & suites in a luxe high-rise offering 10 restaurants & bars, plus a spa, a gym & a pool.
places.name: Palace Hotel Tokyo

sources.shortName: 37 Best Hotels in Tokyo for Ryokan Stays and High-Rise Views
sources.snippet: The legendary property, so named as it’s the closest hotel to the Imperial Palace, lures wealthy Japanese guests with its demure luxury gloss; now, international travelers have gotten wise and are starting to book in as well. Back in the early 2010s, the Palace Hotel doubled down on its commitment to quality and completely demolished its historical property that was erected in the early 1960s in time for the first Tokyo Olympics. A glimmering new luxury stay was born anew, with all the contemporary touches but maintaining its sedate, mod charm born 50 years prior.

sources.shortName: 10 of the best hotels in Tokyo, from charming ryokans to Japanese onsen retreats
sources.snippet: Best for: royal luxuryThis elegant hotel in Otemachi has long been a favourite with well-heeled Tokyoites who come for the dining options and spa. It helps that it’s mere steps away from the Imperial Palace, the city’s most exclusive address, and close to the swish shops of the upmarket Ginza district. Good-sized rooms — some of them featuring balconies — overlook an expanse of moat-carved gardens.

sources.shortName: Best hotels in Tokyo | Telegraph Travel
sources.snippet: The peerless Palace provides guests with the best of both worlds, combining the comforting glamour of a big-city five-star with the care and authenticity of a Japanese-owned independent hotel. Its location overlooking the Imperial Palace Gardens makes it an oasis in a metropolis, and most rooms have the bonus of balconies to make the most of lush views.

sources.shortName: 10 Best 5 Star Hotels in Tokyo
sources.snippet: This is as close as you can get to actually staying on the verdant grounds of the Imperial Palace without being related to the Emperor himself. The architecture and design are as perfectly sober and calm as you'd expect from a high-end Japanese luxury hotel, and the modern-Japanese interiors feel perfectly weighted, carefully considered, expertly crafted. The most basic deluxe rooms are hardly basic at all, and the better ones quickly scale the heights, adding balconies, living rooms, and the like.

places.description: Luxe lodging with swanky rooms & suites, plus 2 upscale restaurants, a chic bar & an indoor pool.
places.name: Shangri-La Tokyo

sources.shortName: Best hotels in Tokyo | Telegraph Travel
sources.snippet: It's all about luxury with a capital L at Shangri-La's Tokyo outpost. The hotel spans the top 11 floors of a 37-storey skyscraper in the Marunouchi district and brims with the signature sparkle of its lavish chandeliers, rich-hued textiles, vast walls of windows, intricate floral arrangements, spacious guestrooms and expansive art collection.

sources.shortName: 12 Best Hotels in Tokyo, Japan
sources.snippet: A favorite of luxury lovers traveling for business and leisure, the Shangri-La Tokyo oozes timeless sophistication. One look at the glimmering crystal chandeliers in the ground-floor reception area and staircase leading to the 28th-floor lobby, and you’ll instantly understand why. It’s formal but not fussy.

sources.shortName: 11 best hotels in Tokyo
sources.snippet: Why stay here: Located adjacent to Tokyo's largest rail station, the property is convenient for those traveling to and from Tokyo's airports, attractions and famous bullet trains to other destinations in Japan.

sources.shortName: The Best Luxury Hotels in Tokyo: 2020 Edition
sources.snippet: Ideal for commuters and those in town for business, Shangri-La Hotel Tokyo offers direct access to Tokyo Station, which is the terminus of the Shinkansen bullet train network and also connects to the city’s local train and subway lines. The luxury high-rise hotel occupies the top 11 floors of the 37-floor Marunouchi Trust Tower Main Building, resulting in unobstructed views of the Marunouchi business area, the Imperial Palace, and beyond. Guests can expect warmly decorated rooms with all the tech amenities you could desire, including Bose audio systems, broadband Internet access and full-sized executive writing desks in every room and suite.

places.description: Elegant quarters in an upmarket hotel offering chic dining, plus a spa & an indoor pool.
places.name: The Tokyo EDITION, Toranomon

sources.shortName: 15 Best Boutique Hotels in Tokyo (2025): Tokyo Edition, Aman Tokyo, & More
sources.snippet: Top amenities: Garden terrace, 24-hour spa, restaurant helmed by Michelin-star chef Tom AikensWhat’s nearby: Luxury shopping district, Ginza, Tokyo Tower. Step onto the 31st-floor reception and you’ll feel like you've entered a cosmopolitan greenhouse—more than 500 trees and plants make their mark as you enter the impressive, minimalist space. Designed by Kengo Kuma, Tokyo Edition is housed in a 38-story skyscraper that exudes elegant calm: Bamboos and ferns make appearances across the common areas and a floating white marble bar twinkles with emerald stools.

sources.shortName: Best hotels in Tokyo | Telegraph Travel
sources.snippet: A jungle-like lobby, minimalist guest rooms, contemporary cuisine, dazzling views and a buzzy creative crowd: The Tokyo EDITION, Toranomon, designed by Kengo Kuma (and Ian Schrager’s firt Japan venture) offers a fresh, modern take on skyscraper luxury in the heart of the city.

sources.shortName: 11 best hotels in Tokyo
sources.snippet: Why stay here: With ample views of iconic landmarks such as the Tokyo Tower and Tokyo Bay, guests will feel immersed in the city — particularly those who book rooms and suites with terraces.

sources.shortName: 17 of the best hotels in Tokyo
sources.snippet: A hotel with a pool is virtually useless in Japan if you have tattoos; while no longer illegal, body art is still frowned upon due to their association with the yakuza (the Japanese mafia), with guests often asked to leave gyms, pools and bath houses. Not so at the Tokyo EDITION, where cocktail maestros in the edgy Gold Bar proudly sport them. Modernity streaks through the rest of the property too, from the indoor jungle that’s the lobby to the spacious rooms in muted colours reminiscent of Scandi-chic and Japanese minimalism.

places.description: Lavish, landmark lodging offering 9 refined restaurants, 2 outdoor pools & a luxe spa.
places.name: Mandarin Oriental, Bangkok

sources.shortName: Our Readers’ Favorite Hotels in Bangkok of 2024
sources.snippet: The high scores in this race indicate just how rich teeming Bangkok is in cosseting retreats. “The property offers a city escape within the city itself,” said one reader of the Capella Bangkok (No. 2). Another praised its cultural activities “that make me feel connected to the local culture.” Across the board, warm service distinguished reader favorites including the Four Seasons Hotel Bangkok at Chao Phraya River (No. 3), about which one voter wrote, “No matter how big or small, everything is taken care of in every possible way.” But it was the historic hall-of-famer Mandarin Oriental, Bangkok that took the top prize.

sources.shortName: The Best Luxury Hotels In Bangkok
sources.snippet: The Mandarin Oriental in Bangkok isn’t just the most luxurious hotel in the city – it’s one of the most luxurious in the world. Set along the banks of the Chao Phraya River, the hotel boasts a 140-year history, and provides its guests with world-class service and amenities. Perks of the hotel include 24-hour butler service, two-Michelin-starred Le Normandie and a one-of-a-kind spa with teak wood treatment rooms and massages that will melt away all your stress.

sources.shortName: 16 Best Hotels in Bangkok (2024)
sources.snippet: The Mandarin Oriental never fails to impress, whether it's your first time or your 40th. The driveway doubles as a garden, and you enter to a teak-and-marble atrium room with birdcage chandeliers and plush rugs. Located in Bang Rak, the hotel is ideal for shopping, transportation, and river activities like dinner cruises and longtail boat rides.

sources.shortName: Ten Bangkok Hotels with Epic River & Skyline Views
sources.snippet: Whenever the subject is Bangkok hotels with river views, one particular establishment inevitably comes up: the five-star, luxurious Mandarin Oriental Bangkok, which is also the city's oldest hotel, with its doors first opening to receive guests in 1876. To guests' delight, some of the hotel's opulent rooms offer truly spectacular Chao Phraya River views: such is the case of the State Rooms, which come with floor-to-ceiling windows and expansive balconies that allow for an unpaired contemplation experience; in turn, these are also enriched with panels made of teak wood and wooden flooring, as well as premium Thai silks that take the signature of Jim Thompson, the American behind rebuilding the silk industry in the country. For an elevated dining experience, head to the best French restaurant in Bangkok, Le Normandie.

places.description: Luxury hotel with chic suites & villas, as well as 3 restaurants, an infinity pool & a spa.
places.name: The Siam

sources.shortName: 16 Best Hotels in Bangkok (2024)
sources.snippet: Compared with many of its rivals, this Bangkok stalwart doesn’t have a location that’s wildly convenient: the postcard sights need a boat transfer, and most top tables are more than a 30-minute taxi ride away. But for me, and the legions of other loyal fans of this monochrome masterpiece by hotel guru Bill Bensley, that’s the point. Pitched up on a lush riverside plot in the hushed Dusit district, The Siam feels like a portal to a bygone Bangkok.

sources.shortName: The Best Luxury Hotels In Bangkok
sources.snippet: Don’t let the out-of-the-way location dissuade you – The Siam is hands down the best boutique hotel in Bangkok. Calling itself an urban sanctuary, the room options – sumptuous suites or pool villas – all come with butler service, espresso machines and portable wifi to help you get around the city. Unique amenities include a movie theatre and a traditional tattoo studio where Thai masters employ the ancient khem (needle) technique.

sources.shortName: 21 of the best hotels in Bangkok
sources.snippet: £££ | SPA | POOL | Best for glamour Set in the upmarket neighbourhood of Dusit, downwater from Bangkok’s historic district, the Siam is a luxurious riverside retreat frequented by Thailand’s high society (known as the hi-so). They come for the designer looks — posing in the fern-filled atrium, by the stripy waterfront swimming pool, on tiger-shaped sofas in the Story House restaurant — and for the excellent spa. Some pick up a permanent souvenir from the hotel’s consecrated Sak Yant tattoo studio.

sources.shortName: Top 10 best luxury hotels in Bangkok
sources.snippet: The Siam hotel – opened in 2013 – is in a category of its own and unique to the Thai capital. With only 39 suites and 3 acres of property along the river, guests are able to experience a resort atmosphere and a level of exclusivity that is not available at Bangkok’s larger luxury properties. The suites at the Siam are amongst the largest in city, all outfitted with plush furnishings, super-sized king beds and lofty ceilings.

places.description: Haute quarters in a posh hotel featuring a 2-floor spa & a tri-level dining & entertainment complex.
places.name: Park Hyatt Bangkok

sources.shortName: The Best Luxury Hotels In Bangkok
sources.snippet: One of the most stunning additions to the Bangkok skyline is the metallic spire of the Park Hyatt, reaching into the clouds like a beacon. This architectural marvel is a mocha-coloured limestone shrine to luxury: decked out with hanging art pieces, it also embraces a saltwater infinity pool, a whisky room with 160 labels and a Pañpuri Organic Spa, with steam and sauna facilities to quell sightseeing-induced aches and pains. Attached to the Central Embassy mall, the hotel is a great bet if your bag is high-end boutiques, restaurants and nightlife, all yours for the taking nearby.

sources.shortName: 16 Best Hotels in Bangkok (2024)
sources.snippet: At Park Hyatt Bangkok, the rooms and common areas were designed by the firm Yabu Pushelberg, which focused on clean, stark lines. The hotel has the feel of an art gallery, where striking design elements surprise you but nothing gets in the way. The Penthouse Bar & Grill, which spans three upper floors of the building, was designed by the famous New York firm of AvroKo.

sources.shortName: Top 10 best luxury hotels in Bangkok
sources.snippet: Embracing its enviable location in one of the world’s most popular tourist destination, Park Hyatt Bangkok offers a refined and uniquely Thai experience, reflecting the country’s rich culture and legendary gracious hospitality. The hotel is housed within Central Embassy, a 37-floor complex that has become one of Bangkok’s most iconic modern landmark since its opening, both because of its futuristic architecture and its ultra-luxury lifestyle mall, which can be directly accessed from the hotel. A devoted team of hosts dedicates themselves to providing Park Hyatt’s world-class discreet and sincere service.

sources.shortName: Ten Bangkok Hotels with Epic River & Skyline Views
sources.snippet: Picture staying in a Bangkok hotel that delivers inspiration from its glorious skyline views and a vast collection of artwork throughout its premises, courtesy of Tos Chirsthivat, Central Group's CEO. Welcome to the extraordinary Park Hyatt Bangkok, a luxury hotel marveling an international clientele since 2017. The hotel has 222 generously sized rooms and suites, starting at 49 square meters, and many boast breathtaking city views. A favorite among guests is the King Corner rooms, allowing for soul-filling 180-degree urban vistas.

places.description: Contemporary rooms & suites in a modern high-rise hotel featuring 6 eateries, 5 bar/lounges & a spa.

sources.shortName: The Best Luxury Hotels In Bangkok
sources.snippet: A head-spinning 21 floors above the Sathorn neighbourhood is the outdoor pool area. For more exertion, there’s the health club, with a range of shape-shifting classes including yoga and Muay Thai. And the spa, with its generous rain showers, is an oasis of signature massages, featuring authentic Thai techniques.

sources.shortName: 21 of the best hotels in Bangkok
sources.snippet: ££ | SPA | POOL | Best for foodiesSoaring above Sathorn, this 61-storey hotel has been delivering top-notch Thai hospitality for the last two decades. Despite the skyscraper setting the hotel feels distinctly Thai, with tropical greenery and traditional music floating through the ground floor lobby, and colourful silk murals and teak accents in the spacious rooms. There are restaurants for every day of the week — Thai, Cantonese, international — as well as stylish dinner cruises on the Chao Phraya River and a scene-stealing rooftop bar made famous in the 2011 comedy blockbuster The Hangover.

sources.snippet: The Banyan Tree’s famous Vertigo Grill and Moon Bar on the 61st floor take the crown as the most spectacular dining venue in Bangkok.” — From our review. Banyan Tree Bangkok is widely regarded as one of the top luxury hotels in Bangkok. It occupies a custom-built high-rise near Silom Road, famous for shopping and entertainment, and boasts elegant interiors that evoke old-world Thai glamour and service that exemplifies Thailand’s warm hospitality.

sources.shortName: 16 Best Hotels in Bangkok (2024)
sources.snippet: The Anantara Siam Bangkok Hotel, which draws a fashionable crowd of international travelers, is a verdant sanctuary in the retail jungle. Much to the delight of those staying here, the property has a stronger resort vibe than many in this area, with tropical landscaping, a central swimming pool, garden terrace rooms, and old-world Thai details. It also offers some of the only terrace rooms in town; they come with adjoining gardens where you can sit out on a private patio.

sources.shortName: The Best Luxury Hotels In Bangkok
sources.snippet: If you want to mingle, you’ve come to the right place: the restaurant and bar outlets of the Anantara Siam are prime territory for the city’s well-heeled. It’s a lavish scene, as you’ll realise, entering the lobby to find priceless artefacts perched atop display cases, creating the impression of both a library and an ornate palace. Choose from Thai, Italian and Japanese for dinner, before heading to al fresco Aqua for a little more people-watching.

sources.shortName: Top 10 best luxury hotels in Bangkok
sources.snippet: Traditional Thai architecture, hand-painted silk ceilings, intricate artwork, an impressively scaled lobby and glorious gardens, the Anantara Siam Bangkok Hotel – a Four Seasons Hotel in an earlier life – offers exquisite accommodations and gracious hospitality strategically located in the corporate, diplomatic and shopping heart of Bangkok’s bustling core. Featuring 340 luxurious, oversized rooms, including 33 suites and eight unique garden cabanas, the property offers exquisite accommodations. The hotel offers seven international choices for dining, ranging from Thai and Italian cuisine to a Japanese eatery and a Manhattan-style grill restaurant  The crowning masterpiece of the hotel is the lobby, which features grand columns with high ceilings adorned by exquisite hand-painted silk panels.

sources.shortName: Best Luxury Hotels In Bangkok, Thailand 2024
sources.snippet: Amenities354 Rooms & Suites, Multiple Restaurants Bars, Spa, Fitness Centre, Outdoor Pool, Butler Service, Club Lounge Access, Chauffeur Service. Found conveniently centrally in the Ratchaprasong neighbourhood, this is Anantara’s flagship urban resort. All of the rooms — from deluxe to club level — feature Jim Thompson fabrics, while suites bring Kasara Executive Lounge privileges.

places.description: Luxury riverfront hotel with 3 chic restaurants, 2 bars & a posh spa, plus an outdoor pool.

sources.shortName: The Best Luxury Hotels In Bangkok
sources.snippet: Pulling up to the ultra-luxe Peninsula, on the west side of the Chao Phraya River, is like travelling through time. The minute you step inside, you’re on first-name terms with staff as they show you the one-of-a-kind spa, world-class restaurants and pool with its view of passing boats. If you want an even more rarefied pick-up, you’re in luck: the Peninsula is the only hotel in the city with its own helipad and door-to-door helicopter service from the airport.

sources.shortName: 16 Best Hotels in Bangkok (2024)
sources.snippet: It feels like you might be in London when you're at The Peninsula in Bangkok's Thonburi neighborhood, thanks to the British racing vehicles parked out front. But the hotel's custom tuk-tuk reminds you that you're in Thailand. Rich, warm, toffee tones carry throughout the lobby and lounges; the space offers grand views over the Chao Praya and the Thai river homes across the water.

sources.shortName: Ten Bangkok Hotels with Epic River & Skyline Views
sources.snippet: Undisputedly, one of the best hotels in Thailand's capital city, The Peninsula Bangkok, located in Khlong San, can be described with adjectives like ornate and sophisticated. Apart from delivering flawless service and captivating decor, this riverside luxury hotel, planted on the opposite margin of the equally spectacular Mandarin Oriental Bangkok, enchants with its mesmerizing river views and skyline panoramas. While the Grand Deluxe rooms, especially those with a balcony, offer spectacular sights, it was the 36-th floor Thai Suite that really captured our attention, with beyond-word vistas of the scintillating Bangkok skyline and the calm waters of the Chao Praya River below.

sources.shortName: 21 of the best hotels in Bangkok
sources.snippet: ££ | SPA | POOL | Best for spa staysThe Peninsula Bangkok has plenty of winning attributes: a wonderful Chao Phraya River location, a beautiful palm-lined outdoor pool, a collection of first-class restaurants and bend-over-backwards service — but what really sets the hotel apart is its splendid spa. Situated in a three-storey colonial mansion within the hotel’s frangipani-scented gardens, it has all kinds of deep-reaching treatments, from traditional Thai massage using thumbs, elbows and knees, to all-day programmes including morning yoga in a nearby temple, Tibetan singing bowls and guided meditation. The therapists here are some of the best in the game.

places.description: Posh rooms & suites with 24/7 butler service in a ritzy hotel offering a spa, a pool & fine dining.

sources.shortName: The Best Luxury Hotels In Bangkok
sources.snippet: Location, location, location: it’s a key part of the St Regis’ appeal. The hotel has its very own BTS Skytrain station for easy (and air-conditioned) access to all parts of the city. Inside, it’s wall-to-wall luxury, with butler service, fine-dining establishments and the brand’s famous afternoon tea.

sources.shortName: 26 Best Hotels in Bangkok
sources.snippet: Lavish and steeped in family traditions, the centrally located St Regis, Bangkok, with direct access to BTS Ratchadamiri, offers 227 spacious rooms (45 sq m to 250 sq m) that blend ornate artwork with contemporary décor and have dramatic views of the Royal Bangkok Sports Club’s golf course and the city’s skyline. Rooms have plenty of character with floor-to-ceiling windows, natural wood floors, lush carpets, plush upholstery, with larger suites sporting generous pantry space for extended stays. Has an exemplary 24 hr bespoke butler service authorized to streamline check-in procedures; they are also available through an e-butler application.

sources.shortName: Top 10 best luxury hotels in Bangkok
sources.snippet: Situated along Bangkoks renowned Rajadamri Road, in the heart of the citys dynamic commercial and business corridor, the St. Regis Bangkok wraps guests in a world of timeless elegance. From the iconic lobby, sweeping views through the floor-to-ceiling windows provide a panoramic of the city’s sparkling skyline, verdant parks, and rolling golf courses. Understated elegance also permeates the 174 guest rooms and 49 suites, which all feature a St. Regis bed with designer fittings meeting the sophisticated Thai-influenced décor.

sources.shortName: The best five star hotels in Bangkok

sources.snippet: Staying true to its worldwide reputation for luxury, the Waldorf Astoria Bangkok pampers its guests from the moment of arrival; a personal concierge takes care of everything you might need. In addition to the 16th-floor pool and soothing spa, there are six dining and drinking outlets, including the Bull & Bear with a menu featuring 55-day dry-aged steaks. Try also mouth-watering French mussels in The Brasserie and fizz in the rooftop Champagne Bar, admiring endless views of the city skyline.

Architect André Fu designed this hotel with bronze accents and soaring ceilings, reflecting the opulence and grandeur of the original Waldorf Astoria Hotel in New York City and cleverly blends Thai charm with luxurious comfort throughout the iconic hotel.

Situated on the ultra-modern Magnolias Ratchadamri Boulevard, the hotel offers a wealth of amenities for discerning business and leisure travelers, including beautifully decorated rooms and suites, great dining options, and indulgent relaxation facilities, which includes a stunning rooftop pool.

sources.shortName: Ten Bangkok Hotels with Epic River & Skyline Views
sources.snippet: Living up to the status of one of the finest hotels in Bangkok, it would be easy to enumerate all the wonders associated with the five-star Waldorf Astoria Bangkok, inaugurated in 2018. Let's jump straight to what is perhaps the hotel's most stunning feature, The Loft and Champagne Bar, reigning over Bangkok from the 56th and 57th floors. Unsurprisingly, the city views here are cinematic and wonderfully combined with an Art Nouveau atmosphere.

sources.snippet: The Grand Hyatt Erawan offers a true five-star experience, from the house Mercedes to the helipad up on the roof. The over-the-top amenities, which make this hotel a favorite among corporate execs and stylish jet-setting families, also include the Erawan Spa Cottages, a cluster of resort-style villa suites that all face gardens. Oversize soaking tubs, rain showers, Nakamichi stereo systems, free-flowing cocktails, and a personal spa concierge are just a few of the many perks.

sources.snippet: The resplendent Raffles Hotel reopened in late 2019 to great fanfare after two years of restoration. Originally built in 1887 as a 10-room hotel, it now features 115 suites with oriental carpets and teak floors to complement four-poster beds and colorful Peranakan-tiled bathrooms. An in-room tablet controls everything from the mood lighting to calling your butler for a glass of bubbly.

sources.shortName: 21 Best Luxury Hotels In Singapore for 2025
sources.snippet: This list would be incomplete without the mention of the Raffles Hotel. Singapore's grande dame is not only a five-star hotel, but it is also a national monument. It was recently overhauled in 2019, and its said to be its most extensive renovations since 1989, with carefully-refurbished suites that maintain their charm.

sources.shortName:

sources.snippet: The team at Raffles’ flagship property know about expectations: they need to operate at the same level as their room rate while managing one of the island’s most feverish tourist attractions (the Singapore Sling was invented on-site, at their monkey-nut-covered Long Bar.) Unsurprisingly then, there’s a performance element to the hotel’s common areas; they even offer to snap a keepsake portrait upon check-in. For us, though, the magic of this 115-key grande dame happens in a quiet garden within Raffles Arcade, that feels a world away from the DSLR shutters: the holistic spa. Perhaps they should put signs up at Changi’s arrival halls, for while the flattering lighting alone would make for a decent jet lag cure, its gemstone massage tops the whole list when it comes to repairing knotty, long-hauled limbs.

sources.shortName: 21 Best Luxury Hotels In Singapore for 2025
sources.snippet: If you’re looking for an ultra-luxe experience to escape reality, make a reservation at Capella, a tropical retreat located in Sentosa, just outside mainland Singapore. Nestled within manicured gardens and lush foliage, the expansive 30-acre resort is the perfect respite. There are rooms, suites, villas, and even manors to choose from, and the bathrooms are stocked with Aesop toiletries.

sources.shortName: The 15 Best Hotels in Singapore to Book Now
sources.snippet: Capella Singapore’s green-fringed patios with private plunge pools are a nice place to relax after a day of hotel-offered activities, like mahjong lessons, cooking classes, or a sidecar tour of the city. Courtesy of Capella Singapore. Refreshed in 2021 by Hong Kong designer André Fu, the 112-room Capella Singapore plays up its idyllic beachfront setting.

sources.shortName: Best Singapore Hotels with a View
sources.snippet: Staying at exclusive Capella Hotel, Singapore is choosing peace and quietness above all - particularly taking into account that the hotel is just moments away from Sentosa's Universal Studios theme park. This super luxurious property is located amidst Sentosa Island's rainforests, in a beautiful 12-hectare landscape area. The hotel is so welcoming that you may feel tempted not to leave: 3 outdoor pools, an award-winning spa (Auriga Spa), exceptional dining options, and a wonderful view onto Singapore's skyline and the sea  - at night, enjoy the ships' twinkling lights like fireflies on the horizon.

sources.snippet: The grand high ceiling, contemporary art collection and opulent-yet-understated décor of The Ritz-Carlton will leave you wondering if you’ve stumbled into a gallery or a hotel. It offers impeccable service including a lavish butler-drawn bath with sweeping views of the marina, spacious rooms, and complimentary wired and wireless internet access so you can always stay plugged in. You won’t go hungry either.

sources.shortName: The 15 Best Hotels in Singapore to Book Now
sources.snippet: A superlative Ritz-Carlton with a La Mer Spa, a Michelin-starred restaurant, and art by Warhol, Chihuly, and Stella. Its sumptuous rooms with octagonal, feng shui approved, bay-facing bathroom windows and butler-drawn baths indicate five-star luxury.

sources.shortName: 21 Best Luxury Hotels In Singapore for 2025

sources.shortName: The 15 Best Hotels in Singapore to Book Now
sources.snippet: What was once Clifford Pier, a landing point for immigrants arriving in Singapore, is now a snazzy hotel welcoming well-heeled travelers. Located right on the water and clad in glass and metal, the 100-room Fullerton Bay Hotel Singapore feels glamorous with a heady scent of gardenias and lilies wafting through its dramatically arched hallways. The plush rooms designed by Andre Fu boast views of the Marina Bay Sands, Customs House, or Clifford Pier; the Premier Bay View rooms offer a private deck and Jacuzzi overlooking Marina Bay.

sources.shortName: 21 Best Luxury Hotels In Singapore for 2025
sources.snippet: Clifford Pier, one of Fullerton Bay Hotel Singapore's two heritage wings was once the landing point for immigrants to Singapore. So it's fitting, then, that the hotel pays homage to that history by dedicating its suites to showcase each of Singapore's cultural identities. The Robinson Suite is chinoiserie chic, all decked with silk panels and throws, and decorated with Ming era-inspired vases.

Ruby-hued Lantern is one of the coolest rooftop bars in the city, set next to a giant swimming pool — both have pinch-me views of the city.

During my 6 months living in Singapore, I had to take a staycation in Marina Bay Sands, the rooftop pool is so surreal and an amazing place to unwind after a day exploring in the muggy heat.

sources.snippet: Four Seasons Hotel Singapore is an oasis of calm amidst bustling Singapore. All decked out in elegant furnishing surrounded by Asian antiques, this suite is a tranquil space along the tree-lined Orchard Boulevard – complete with an incredible view of the city skyline.

sources.shortName: 26 Best Hotels in Singapore, From Tropical Villas to Luxe Grand Dames
sources.snippet: We love the fact that the staff never fails to make you feel welcome; with a detailed database on all its guests and their preferences, they can predict your needs.
